name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment I
measures: Large-scale flame spread in an uncrewed Cygnus
safety: Shows how a bigger fire grows inside a real spacecraft

name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment II
measures: Burn length in microgravity vs 1g for the same samples
safety: Direct 0-g vs 1-g comparison of material flammability

name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment III
measures: Flame spread at higher airflow (30 cm/s)
safety: Ventilation speed effect on a large fire

name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME and SAME-R)
fuel: Kapton, Teflon, silicone, lamp wick, Pyrell, DBP
measures: Smoke particle size and concentration from overheated materials
safety: Sets what a spacecraft smoke detector must sense

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids II
fuel: PMMA films, rods, slabs; SIBAL; Nomex
measures: Burns in low-speed flow; O2, CO2, CO before and after
safety: Material flammability and gas build-up in a sealed volume

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids
fuel: SIBAL, PMMA spheres and slabs, wax
measures: Burns in low-speed flow with nitrogen suppression; crew observations

name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
measures: Extinction and burning rate vs O2, pressure, CO2, He
safety: Limits of flammability and suppressant effectiveness

name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment 2
fuel: Octane, heptane, decane, ethanol droplets and mixtures
safety: Extends FLEX to more fuels and up to 30% O2

name: White Sands 1-g oxygen flammability thresholds (Hirsch 2011)
fuel: PET, PEI, silicone, polyimide, PEEK, PMMA, PVC, nylon and others
measures: Upward limiting oxygen index (ULOI) and maximum oxygen concentration (MOC) in 1 g
safety: Ground-test thresholds that microgravity results are compared against

name: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
safety: When a flame starts releasing soot

name: Cool Flames Investigation
safety: A flame can look out and still be burning

name: Burning Rate Emulator
fuel: Gas burner emulating solids and liquids

name: Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
